The manuscripts, datasets and atlas present one current research account. This page explains its classification scope, remaining questions and the limits of the available verification.

AI-generated research · independent verification pending

The results, proofs, code and data have not yet been independently verified by human experts or formalized in Lean. Treat them as provisional. Automated checks and separate AI reviews establish only their stated scope.

“Realized,” “excluded” and “complete” describe the project’s recorded claims. They do not certify that a proof has received human or proof-assistant verification.

The remaining mathematical questions

Rank six · R6_4_155

Rank six · R6_4_155

The necessary center data determine a rank-52 candidate with a rank-26 modular factor. Every odd generalized pivotal rotation must factor through a cyclic spin character; all 1,144 tested blocks pass this condition. The all-order path-Clifford divisibility condition for the family R′(m) holds exactly when m is even, including m = 4. These constraints do not provide compatible associators or a categorification, and no general exclusion is established.

Rank six · R6_8_1660

Rank six · R6_8_1660

In the established positive spherical representative, saturated modular representations determine all indicator sequences and central phase masses. The eight spin objects form four dual pairs with a common restriction vector. Exact phase Gram constraints leave 640 labelled restriction-data profiles, in three branches of 68, 286 and 286. These are necessary data; they neither construct nor exclude a categorification.

Rank eight · current results and research history

Rank eight · multiplicity three

The 3,527 exact-multiplicity-three rings have 3,507 general exclusions, 16 unitary models and four unresolved cases: R8_3_928, R8_3_941, R8_3_1154 and R8_3_1768.

These four admit sphericality and Galois pseudo-unitarity reductions and have no braided Morita representative. Their necessary center data do not establish categorifiability. R928 has categorical Morita rigidity. For R1768 an actual twisted GH(C6,2) precursor now exists, but the required algebra 1+sigma remains unproved. R8_3_436 is separately excluded by its new spherical-equivariantization proof; the old TPE parameterization remains withdrawn.

Rank eight · earlier inner-square obstruction

Rank eight · inner-square rigidity

A categorification of R8_2_24 would supply a tensor autoequivalence whose square is conjugation by a specified invertible object. Forced Frobenius–Schur signs constrain its action on two-dimensional fusion spaces. The short weights of all associator coefficients then force a continuous family of inequivalent tensor autoequivalences, contradicting tensor-functor rigidity. The argument applies to arbitrary complex categorifications after the justified Galois reduction.

The rank-eight manuscript gives the full proof. Separate AI reviews checked the categorical signs, common choices of bases, conductor reduction and rigidity argument. Exact checks bind the source tensor and verify the finite weight calculation. Independent human verification and Lean formalization remain pending.

Rank nine · multiplicity two

Rank nine · multiplicity two

All 2,083 supplied tensors have source-bound decisions: 2,043 general exclusions, 36 unitary models and four unresolved rings. Ten exclusions and four coherent constructions settle fourteen cases from the earlier publication.

The remaining cases are R9_2_137, R9_2_1607, R9_2_1975 and R9_2_1976. All have no braided categorification. General existence reduces to pseudo-unitary existence after the audited sphericalization/Galois step; this does not make every original category pseudo-unitary or unitary. The necessary D8 Morita rings have three types in their union. New stabilizer and Clifford theorems sharpen their cubic spectra; compatible associators and inverse modules remain unknown.

What the checks establish

The verification separates mathematical hypotheses and cited theorems from exact tensor calculations, finite certificates, source hashes and publication checks. A computation can verify an identity; the categorical argument explaining why the identity applies requires a mathematical proof.

Exact checks cover fusion-ring axioms, classification-ledger consistency, certificate replay and manuscript/download checksums. The verification guide gives commands, prerequisites and the scope of each check. The verification report records the detailed coverage.

Rank-six computational coverage

The current correction route retains all original raw exclusion verdicts, complete reference-backend retries and the exact post-loop checks. The eleven immutable multiplicity-nine proofs run in their source-compatible frozen context, with current tensor and certificate identities checked. This is an explicitly source-bound combined campaign, not a single uniform-backend invocation.

Independent review is still needed

The most delicate arguments concern categorical coherence, simultaneous diagram conventions, sphericalization and conductor-equality refinements. Passing arithmetic checks is not a substitute for establishing those steps. The verification report identifies specific expert-review priorities and the remaining limits.

If you find an error, a repository issue naming the ring, theorem and precise failing step will support a precise mathematical review.
